models.name: URL Journey
models.description: Follow one HTTPS request across DNS, routing, transport, TLS, HTTP, packets, failures, and recovery.

frames.title: Navigate to example.test
frames.summary: The application turns a human hostname into a network dependency graph.

frames.title: DNS cache miss
frames.summary: No usable cached answer exists for this curated journey.

frames.title: Stub asks recursive resolver
frames.summary: A recursive A query is issued for example.test.

frames.title: Root referral received
frames.summary: The recursive resolver learns where to continue the namespace walk.

frames.title: TLD referral received
frames.summary: The recursive resolver is directed toward the authoritative zone.

frames.title: example.test → 203.0.113.42
frames.summary: The authoritative answer supplies a documentation-only destination address for the deterministic story.

frames.title: Answer cached
frames.summary: The recursive result becomes reusable until its simulated TTL expires.

frames.title: Destination enters the routing table
frames.summary: 203.0.113.42 requires a next-hop decision outside the local subnet.

frames.title: Default gateway selected
frames.summary: The host has a viable local path to the router that can forward toward the Internet.

frames.title: Interdomain path context appears
frames.summary: A simulated valley-free AS path carries the story beyond the local routing domain.

frames.title: Physical infrastructure comes into view
frames.summary: Interconnection facilities give geography to the story without claiming a cable or exact forwarding path.

frames.title: SYN leaves the client
frames.summary: TCP opens a reliable byte stream before TLS begins.

frames.title: SYN-ACK returns
frames.summary: The server acknowledges the client sequence space and contributes its own initial sequence number.

frames.title: TCP connection established
frames.summary: The third handshake segment makes the bidirectional byte stream usable.

frames.title: ClientHello
frames.summary: SNI names example.test; ALPN offers h2.

frames.title: ServerHello
frames.summary: The server selects compatible cryptographic parameters and contributes its key share.

frames.title: Handshake traffic becomes encrypted
frames.summary: EncryptedExtensions and later server handshake messages are protected with handshake keys.

frames.title: Certificate identity validated
frames.summary: The presented identity is checked against example.test.

frames.title: Application traffic keys ready
frames.summary: Both sides can now protect application data with TLS 1.3 application traffic secrets.

frames.title: HTTP/2 control state exchanged
frames.summary: SETTINGS establishes connection-level HTTP/2 parameters over the encrypted stream.

frames.title: GET / on example.test
frames.summary: Request headers become an encrypted HTTP/2 HEADERS frame carried by TLS over TCP.

frames.title: Application data isolated
frames.summary: HTTP/2 request headers for GET / on example.test becomes the logical payload.

frames.title: TLS 1.3 application data closes
frames.summary: HTTP/2 request bytes become opaque TLS application data.

frames.title: TCP segment assembles
frames.summary: TCP ports, sequence space, flags, window, and checksum surround the protected bytes.

frames.title: IPv4 envelope assembles
frames.summary: Source, destination, TTL, protocol, length, and checksum establish the routed packet.

frames.title: Hop-local Ethernet envelope closes
frames.summary: Source and next-hop destination MAC addresses frame the same IPv4 packet for this local link.

frames.title: Structured frame ready at the NIC
frames.summary: Five semantic representations collapse into one deterministic outbound data unit.

frames.title: NIC serializes the structured frame
frames.summary: The frame becomes an ordered link transmission without changing its packet semantics.

frames.title: Symbols cross the access link
frames.summary: Structured bytes become physical link activity moving toward the switch.

frames.title: Switch isolates destination MAC
frames.summary: Only the destination MAC is projected for the forwarding decision; unrelated packet fields recede.

frames.title: MAC table selects Gi0/24
frames.summary: The same Ethernet header and IPv4 payload leave the selected switch port.

frames.title: Router terminates the incoming Ethernet envelope
frames.summary: The hop-local Layer 2 shell opens and ends; the routed IPv4 packet remains.

frames.title: TTL decrements: 64 → 63
frames.summary: The router mutates the IPv4 TTL and updates the IPv4 header checksum.

frames.title: Destination IP selects the next hop
A new Ethernet envelope assembles
frames.summary: Router wan0 constructs new source and next-hop destination MAC fields around the forwarded IPv4 packet.

frames.title: The re-encapsulated packet continues
frames.summary: A second link transmission carries the new Ethernet frame toward 198.51.100.2.

frames.title: Response headers arrive
frames.summary: The origin begins the response with status and metadata before the body streams.

frames.title: Response DATA streams
frames.summary: Encrypted application data crosses the established TCP stream.

frames.title: Freeze one TCP frame
frames.summary: One delivery unit becomes the entire world: link, network, transport, and encrypted TLS payload bytes.

frames.title: Explode TCP/IP headers
frames.summary: The same frame opens into persistent link, network, transport, security, and application objects.

frames.title: Transfer acknowledged
frames.summary: The representative response flight is cumulatively acknowledged and TCP delivery is complete.

frames.title: Response available to the application
frames.summary: Decrypted response bytes are delivered upward to the browser.

frames.title: Pull back through the route
frames.summary: The journey recedes from application state to the forwarding structures that carried it.

frames.title: Return to Internet scale
frames.summary: Local routes, AS policy, and physical infrastructure collapse back into one global context.

frames.title: example.test journey complete
frames.summary: A human hostname became DNS state, routing state, transport state, protected application traffic, packets, and finally a response.

models.name: Failure Story
models.description: Fail the active route and watch convergence, recomputation, failover, and the causal chain unfold.

frames.title: Primary path established
frames.summary: Application traffic is flowing through R1 on the lowest-cost route.

frames.title: Primary link fails
frames.summary: The R1 ↔ CORE adjacency disappears and the forwarding path is broken.

frames.title: R1 floods new link state
frames.summary: R1 advertises that the R1 ↔ CORE link is no longer reachable.

frames.title: Failure knowledge propagates
frames.summary: R2 and CORE now share the updated topology view.

frames.title: SPF selects the alternate path
frames.summary: The failed edge is removed from the graph and the standby route through R2 wins.

frames.title: Forwarding moves to R2
frames.summary: New traffic leaves the edge router on the alternate next hop.

frames.title: Traffic recovers
frames.summary: The application flow is healthy again over the alternate route.

models.name: TCP Theater
models.description: Handshake, sequence space, loss, retransmission, congestion response, and teardown.

frames.title: Client opens the connection
frames.summary: SYN consumes one sequence number and proposes CLIENT ISN 1000.

frames.title: Server answers with SYN / ACK
frames.summary: SERVER ISN 7000 acknowledges the client SYN with ACK 1001.

frames.title: Connection established
frames.summary: ACK 7001 completes the three-way handshake.

frames.title: Segment 1 arrives in order
frames.summary: SEQ 1001–2460 advances the receiver next-expected byte to 2461.

frames.title: Segment 2 is lost
frames.summary: SEQ 2461–3920 disappears before the server receives it.

frames.title: Segment 3 arrives out of order
frames.summary: SEQ 3921–5380 arrives, but byte 2461 is still missing.

frames.title: Duplicate ACK 1
frames.summary: The server repeats ACK 2461: that is still the first missing byte.

frames.title: Segment 4 extends the out-of-order queue
frames.summary: SEQ 5381–6840 arrives while the 2461 hole remains.

frames.title: Duplicate ACK 2
frames.summary: ACK 2461 repeats again.

frames.title: Segment 5 arrives behind the same hole
frames.summary: SEQ 6841–8300 arrives out of order.

frames.title: Duplicate ACK 3 triggers fast retransmit
frames.summary: The third ACK 2461 crosses the curated Reno fast-retransmit threshold.

frames.title: Reno enters fast recovery
frames.summary: ssthresh falls to 3 MSS; cwnd is temporarily inflated to 6 MSS.

frames.title: Fast retransmit repairs the hole
frames.summary: SEQ 2461–3920 is sent again immediately.

frames.title: One ACK releases the buffered ranges
frames.summary: ACK 8301 cumulatively covers segments 2 through 5.

frames.title: cwnd deflates to ssthresh
frames.summary: Fast recovery ends at cwnd 3 MSS, ssthresh 3 MSS.

frames.title: Forward progress resumes
frames.summary: SEQ 8301–9760 crosses the repaired connection.

frames.title: ACK 9761 grows the window again
frames.summary: Successful delivery raises the illustrated congestion window to 4 MSS.

frames.title: Client begins teardown
frames.summary: FIN at SEQ 9761 consumes one final sequence number.

frames.title: Server acknowledges and closes its side
frames.summary: ACK 9762 plus FIN at SERVER SEQ 7001.

frames.title: Final ACK closes the theater sequence
frames.summary: ACK 7002 confirms the server FIN.

models.name: DNS Theater
models.description: Recursive resolution, cache behavior, TTLs, retries, and visible failure boundaries.

frames.title: Stub asks for a recursive answer
frames.summary: www.example.test A leaves the client with RD=1.

frames.title: Recursive cache misses
frames.summary: No usable answer or delegation is cached for this teaching query.

frames.title: Recursive asks the root
frames.summary: Who knows www.example.test?

frames.title: Root refers the resolver to .test
frames.summary: The answer is not here; the next authority is the test. TLD.

frames.title: Recursive follows the .test delegation
frames.summary: The same www.example.test A question moves one level deeper.

frames.title: .test refers to example.test
frames.summary: The authoritative nameserver for example.test is the next stop.

frames.title: Recursive reaches the authoritative zone
frames.summary: Now the resolver asks the server that owns example.test.

frames.title: Authoritative answer returns
frames.summary: www.example.test → 203.0.113.42 · TTL 300s

frames.title: Recursive caches the answer
frames.summary: A 203.0.113.42 enters cache with 300s remaining.

frames.title: Recursive returns the completed answer
frames.summary: 203.0.113.42 reaches the stub resolver.

frames.title: Miss path complete
frames.summary: Four network exchanges produced one cached answer.

models.name: TLS 1.3 Theater
models.description: Handshake negotiation, key schedule, certificate boundary, and encrypted application data.

frames.title: Client offers TLS 1.3 parameters
frames.summary: SNI www.example.test, ALPN h2/http1.1, X25519 key share, and TLS 1.3 cipher suites leave in the clear.

frames.title: Server selects the cryptographic context
frames.summary: TLS 1.3, X25519, and TLS_AES_128_GCM_SHA256 are selected.

frames.title: Handshake traffic secrets become available
frames.summary: ECDHE feeds the Handshake Secret; transcript(ClientHello…ServerHello) contextualizes client/server handshake traffic secrets.

frames.title: The handshake crosses the encryption boundary
frames.summary: EncryptedExtensions is the first server handshake message protected with server handshake traffic keys.

frames.title: Server sends its simulated certificate chain
frames.summary: www.example.test leaf → HOPSCOTCH Test Intermediate → HOPSCOTCH Test Root.

fields.label: Root
fields.value: HOPSCOTCH Test Root · simulated trust anchor

frames.title: Server proves possession of the certificate key
frames.summary: A signature covers the TLS 1.3 CertificateVerify context and the handshake transcript.

frames.title: Client validates identity and chain
frames.summary: Hostname www.example.test matches; simulated chain and CertificateVerify proof validate.

frames.title: Server authenticates the handshake transcript
frames.summary: Server Finished verifies the handshake state and completes the server authentication block.

frames.title: Master and application traffic secrets are derived
frames.summary: The transcript through server Finished feeds client/server application traffic secret 0.

frames.title: Client Finished completes mutual key confirmation
frames.summary: The client Finished is still protected with client handshake traffic keys.

frames.title: HTTP/2 request is now opaque TLS Application Data
frames.summary: The record layer uses client application traffic secret 0 derived key/IV material.

frames.title: Server responds under application traffic keys
frames.summary: Encrypted TLS records carry the HTTP/2 response in the opposite direction.

frames.title: Authenticated encrypted channel established
frames.summary: TLS 1.3 negotiation, server authentication, Finished verification, and application-key transition are complete.

models.name: HTTP/2 vs HTTP/3
models.description: Compare multiplexing, TCP head-of-line blocking, QUIC streams, and recovery behavior.

frames.title: Two responses begin concurrently
frames.summary: Both lanes serve /hero.jpg and /app.js at the same time.

records.label: HTTP/2
records.value: H2 streams 1 + 3 share one ordered TCP byte stream

records.label: HTTP/3
records.value: H3 request streams 0 + 4 are independent QUIC streams

frames.title: Both resources make forward progress
frames.summary: Initial data for both streams reaches the client in both lanes.

records.label: HTTP/2
records.value: TCP delivers bytes in order to HTTP/2

records.label: HTTP/3
records.value: QUIC delivers ordered bytes within each stream

frames.title: The same logical Stream A data is lost
frames.summary: A transport packet carrying /hero.jpg data disappears in each lane.

records.label: HTTP/2
records.value: TCP sequence hole opens in the connection byte stream

records.label: HTTP/3
records.value: QUIC Stream A offset range is missing

frames.title: Later data arrives after the gap
frames.summary: Packets carrying later bytes—including Stream B data—still reach the receiver.

records.label: HTTP/2
records.value: Later TCP bytes are buffered behind the missing sequence range

records.label: HTTP/3
records.value: Stream B bytes can be delivered independently of Stream A ordering

frames.title: The lanes visibly diverge
frames.summary: HTTP/2 stalls both responses; HTTP/3 keeps /app.js moving.

records.label: HTTP/2
records.value: CONNECTION HOL · Stream A + Stream B blocked

records.label: HTTP/3
records.value: Stream A blocked · Stream B still progressing

frames.title: QUIC loss still affects the connection
frames.summary: HTTP/3 avoids cross-stream ordering blockage, not all consequences of packet loss.

records.label: HTTP/2
records.value: TCP loss recovery / congestion response active

records.label: HTTP/3
records.value: QUIC loss recovery active · Stream B remains deliverable

frames.title: TCP retransmits the missing connection bytes
frames.summary: Repairing the TCP sequence hole finally lets HTTP/2 see the buffered later bytes.

records.label: HTTP/2
records.value: TCP retransmission repairs the connection byte stream

records.label: HTTP/3
records.value: Stream B has already moved ahead

frames.title: HTTP/2 releases both stalled streams
frames.summary: /hero.jpg and /app.js jump forward together after TCP repair.

records.label: HTTP/3
records.value: No equivalent cross-stream release event was necessary

frames.title: QUIC repairs Stream A
frames.summary: /hero.jpg receives the missing stream range while /app.js is already near completion.

records.label: HTTP/2
records.value: Both H2 streams are progressing again

records.label: HTTP/3
records.value: Only Stream A needed ordering repair

frames.title: Both lanes complete
frames.summary: The final payload bytes are the same; the delivery coupling under loss was not.

records.label: HTTP/3
records.value: HTTP/3 complete with independent stream progress
